This vignette walks through the full cavefindr pipeline (correcting cave
coordinates, training a model, and predicting new cave entrances) using a
small example dataset that comes with the package. The functions produce 
some diagnostic plots that might appear in RStudio's "Plots", hidden by 
the vignette.

## Setup

Pick or create a working directory to store an output folder: 
that's where `correct_coordinates()`, `train_model()`, and `get_predictions()` will save their results.

```{r setup}
library(cavefindr)
```

## Get the example data

`get_example_las()` and `get_example_cave_dataset()` read the 
example LAS tile and cave coordinate dataset into memory.

```{r get-data}
my_las <- get_example_las()
my_las
lidR::plot(my_las)
lidR::las_check(my_las)

my_cave_dataset <- get_example_cave_dataset()
my_cave_dataset
```

The example data simulates a small (200 x 200 m) LiDAR tile with 3 narrow, deep depressions that are clearly detectable in the pointcloud, 1 shallow depression that is not detectable, and a cave coordinate dataset with the GPS-error-affected location of each of the above, plus one point that falls entirely outside the LAS tile.

## Check a coordinate

`check_coordinate()` lets you look at the pointcloud around any single coordinate.

```{r check-coordinate}
check_coordinate(
  x = -50347.3,
  y = -12417.2,
  las = my_las,
  radius = 10
)
```

## Correct cave coordinates

`correct_coordinates()` takes the cave database and, for each
point, looks for the true entrance location in the pointcloud within the set radius.
You'll be asked if each of the 5 points is detectable in the pointcloud, since the 
function can only correct caves which are detectable.

```{r correct-coordinates}
my_cave_rois_corrected <- correct_coordinates(
  cave_vect = my_cave_dataset,
  las = my_las,
  radius = 10,
  review = TRUE
)
```

## Train a model

`train_model()` computes a set of metrics for each
corrected cave ROI plus an equal number of random background ROIs, and
trains a random forest classifier to distinguish them. You can pass the object
returned by `correct_coordinates()` directly, or its export id.

```{r train-model}
my_model <- train_model(
  corrected_rois = my_cave_rois_corrected,
  las = my_las,
  metrics = c(
    "depth_plane",
    "depth_mean",
    "depth_half_radius_mean",
    "depth_w_mean",
    "slope",
    "intensity",
    "NIR"
  ),
  plot = TRUE,
  var_imp = TRUE
)
```

## Predict new cave entrances

`get_predictions()` scans a LAS tile for candidate cave entrances, either
using the trained model (`method = "model"`) or simple mechanistic
thresholds (`method = "simple"`). With `inspection = TRUE`, each candidate
is shown to you for manual inspection and labeling of each point.

```{r predict-model}
get_predictions(
  method = "model",
  las = my_las,
  model = my_model,
  score_threshold = 0.5,
  isolated_policy = "include",
  remove_edges = TRUE,
  remove_waterlines = TRUE,
  inspection = TRUE
)
```

```{r predict-simple}
get_predictions(
  method = "simple",
  las = my_las,
  metric_thresholds = list(depth_plane = 2),
  radius = 10,
  isolated_policy = "include",
  remove_edges = TRUE,
  remove_waterlines = TRUE,
  inspection = TRUE
)
```
